summary: Backend-only regression tests for Ledger by Arsonist. Built pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covering all requested flows: registration (OTP happy path + 11 starter categories, dup 409, short-pw 422, wrong OTP 400, 5-wrong->429), login (success, wrong pw 401, 5+wrong->429 lockout), refresh token rotation + single-use reuse denial, logout revocation, /auth/me (401 without auth, no password_hash leak, PATCH aliases merge with defaults), change-password (wrong current 401, correct rotates and invalidates old), forgot/reset (unknown email 200 without dev_otp, full reset invalidates old pw & old refresh tokens), ledger CRUD for accounts/cards/categories/subcategories/transactions with filters (?month, ?type) and /transactions/months, budgets PUT upsert (same monthKey+categoryId+subcategoryId updates amount, does not duplicate), soft-delete tombstones and 404 on subsequent PATCH, per-user scoping (user B gets 404 on user A's ids), client-supplied ids (bank_custom_*) + 409 on duplicate, sync full pull, incremental pull with tombstone flag deleted:true, last-write-wins (older updated_at not applied), invalid item -> rejected with reason, export /json and /csv (text/csv + header row + rows), /data/reset restores 11 starter categories, DELETE /auth/me (requires password, subsequent login fails), POST /auth/google -> 503, GET /api/health -> 200. All 29 tests PASS.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout is keyed on request.client.host+email. Behind K8s ingress this resolves to the ingress pod IP (observed 10.208.134.74 and .75 alternating per request), so an attacker's fails split across multiple pod-IP buckets. Effective attempts-before-lockout ~= 5 * (#ingress pods). Should honor X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP (with a trusted-proxy allowlist) so the true client IP is used. Test had to fire up to 15 attempts to guarantee 429.
Response emails are lowercased server-side (correct) but the client receives a lowercased echo -- fine, just documenting expectation for FE.

OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 with `attempts >= MAX` check means the code accepts 5 wrong submissions (each returns 400) and the 6th returns 429. Matches spec intent but worth documenting: it's 'up to 5 wrong tries, then next request is locked'.

action_items: Consider fixing lockout key to derive real client IP from X-Forwarded-For (behind trusted proxy) instead of request.client.host, otherwise brute-force protection is weakened proportionally to the number of ingress replicas.
(Optional) Add a rate limit / cooldown on /auth/forgot-password to avoid spam OTP generation for known emails.
(Optional) /auth/register/request-otp always returns 502 if send fails but in dev mode send is a no-op -- fine as-is.
critical_code_review_comments: security.py check_lockout uses request.client.host which is ingress pod IP in K8s -- lockout is bypassable by natural load-balancing.

auth.py _consume_otp: after MAX attempts it returns 429 and deletes the OTP doc; but a 6th call is required to trigger the delete (attempts already stored=5 on the 5th failed call). Acceptable but a bit non-obvious.

ledger.py _create: uses replace_one upsert=True after a find_one check -- theoretically race-y for concurrent duplicate POSTs on the same client-supplied id (would silently overwrite). Consider a unique-index-driven insert to raise DuplicateKey instead.

sync.push validates payload with the same *In models, which require full field sets. If a client pushes a partial update it will land in `rejected`. Consider allowing partial (PATCH-like) semantics if that is desired for offline updates -- otherwise document that push items must be complete.

sync.push last-write-wins comparison uses raw string > on ISO timestamps (`existing.updated_at > incoming_ts`) -- correct for RFC3339 ISO but fragile if a client sends a differently formatted stamp. Consider parsing to datetime.
export.csv sorts by t['date'] but does not handle missing dates; validators guarantee non-null so fine.

starter_data.py: starter category ids are fixed strings ('cat_income', 'sub_salary', ...). If two users exist they will share the same category ids in different scopes, which is fine (scoped by user_id) but couples client code to those constants -- document them as stable.
server.py CORS: allow_credentials=True with explicit origins from CORS_ORIGINS -- good. No wildcard.
get_current_user also accepts token via `access_token` cookie -- unusual for a mobile-only API. Confirm this is intentional (used by any web client).
test_credentials: Seeded: jyothi.test@example.com / secret123. All other users are created on-the-fly per test via request-otp dev_otp flow.
seed_data_creation: No manual seeding. Each test creates its own TEST_-prefixed user (email) and its own scoped ledger data. Users are largely left in place (except the delete-me test which removes its own user).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend URL: https://063094db-01fa-40c3-b295-3bce7899da87.preview.emergentagent.com/api. Registration uses dev_otp in response (RESEND_API_KEY empty). Google endpoint returns 503 by design. Lockout is IP+email so use fresh emails per lockout test AND fire >=~10 attempts (ingress LB across replicas splits the counter). Sync push validates each item against the entity's *In pydantic model; partial payloads are rejected. Soft-deleted docs are visible via /sync/pull as deleted:true tombstones (needed for LWW). /auth/me PATCH always merges DEFAULT_ALIASES={Work:Work, Personal:Personal} on top of any input.
rca of the issue: Lockout weakened by ingress-behind-K8s: request.client.host resolves to the ingress pod IP (observed alternating 10.208.134.74/.75 in login_attempts docs), so 5 attempts from a single attacker split across N docs and never hit the 429 threshold until 5*N attempts. Fix: read the leftmost value of X-Forwarded-For (or X-Real-IP) when a trusted proxy is configured, and use that as the identifier.
